title: 'I'm going to drive': FAA outage and high fares reshape Thanksgiving travel plans
summary: NEW YORK, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Dinese Jackson couldn't stomach spending roughly $1,500 to fly herself and her two children from Raleigh, North Carolina, to Dallas, Texas, for Thanksgiving, more than double what she had paid for similar trips in the past. Still, she kept checking airfares in hopes fares would ‌drop, until the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop on November 13 cemented her decision to make the trip by car instead, even at the price of a ‌17-hour drive.
